items.title: The name
items.text: zanybrainy.com was live when we read it in October 2026. It sells a handful of Zany Brainy-branded items, among them a T-shirt, a backpack, a notebook and stickers, and its “Our Story” page speaks of sharing “a small glimpse of the past.” The pages carry the line “© 2025 ZANY BRAINY” and name no company. We could not establish who owns the trademark or how it left FAO Inc.’s estate.[^26]

items.title: The original company
items.text: Zany Brainy, Inc. sold its business in September 2001 and stayed in Chapter 11 as a shell. A liquidating plan was confirmed on March 6, 2002 and every share was cancelled. It ended its SEC registration two weeks later.[^10][^29]

items.title: The stores
items.text: FAO Inc. had engaged liquidators by December 2, 2003 and filed for Chapter 11 on December 4 “to liquidate their Zany Brainy business in an orderly manner.” It said the wind-down would be completed early in 2004. What became of the 89 leases is not in our sources.[^17][^25]

items.title: The sister chains
items.text: FAO Inc., renamed Children’s Books & Toys, Inc., filed two asset purchase agreements in February 2004: one for the FAO Schwarz business, dated January 23, 2004, and one for The Right Start, dated December 15, 2003. No agreement for Zany Brainy is among them.[^28]

items.title: The founder and the last chief executive
items.text: David Schlessinger and Thomas Vellios founded Five Below in 2002, a chain selling goods priced at $5 and under to teenagers. It went public in July 2012, when it had 199 stores (as of April 28, 2012), more than Zany Brainy ever had.[^27]

items.title: The creditors
items.text: The Waterton deal of July 2001 was expected to pay unsecured creditors 15 to 20 cents on the dollar. Under The Right Start’s deal they were to share $7.5M in cash and 1.1 million Right Start shares. What they finally received is not in our sources.[^8][^11]

blocks.title: Who owned the name
blocks.subtitle: Two public companies, three bankruptcies, and an online shop that does not say whose it is.

nodes.what: Founded by David Schlessinger. First store in Wynnewood, Pennsylvania.[^3][^27]
Listed on Nasdaq at $10.00 a share.[^1]
Buys substantially all the assets through its subsidiary ZB Company, Inc.[^10][^11]
The Right Start renames itself after buying FAO Schwarz. 169 Zany Brainy stores.[^12][^24]
Closes 80 Zany Brainy stores and emerges in April with 89.[^13][^14]
Files to liquidate Zany Brainy and sell its other two chains.[^17]
zanybrainy.com sells branded merchandise. Ownership of the trademark is unknown to us.[^26]

blocks.source: SEC filings of Zany Brainy, Inc. and of The Right Start, Inc. / FAO Inc.[^1][^5][^10][^11][^12][^13][^14][^17], Publishers Weekly[^24] and zanybrainy.com[^26].
